children: Samsung Electronics (SSNLF), the memory-chip and consumer-electronics powerhouse, put an estimated ?90 trillion to ?110 trillion shareholder-return program in the spotlight Thursday. The stock closed 0.2% lower at ?269,000 in Seoul as investors waited for a clearer answer on how the technology giant will deploy its mountain of AI-driven cash.

Roughly ?30 trillion will be paid through third-quarter cash dividends, while Samsung expects to decide the rest of the distribution in January. Management has kept buybacks and share cancellations on the table, but investors wanted something firmer. Dividends return cash. Repurchases followed by cancellations also shrink the share countand that distinction matters when shareholders are pushing for a stronger response to undervaluation and ownership concerns.

The confirmed dividend represents only about 30% of the program's ?100 trillion midpoint, leaving most of the capital-allocation story unwritten. The picture reinforces the tension: Samsung carries an impressive GF Score of 92 out of 100, powered by strong growth, profitability and financial strength, while GF Value remains its weakest category. Samsung has the cash and operating muscle; investors now want a payout structure capable of unlocking more of that strength.

title: Samsung's ?100 Trillion Payout Still Leaves Investors Demanding Buybacks
